extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (patent agents and attorneys) before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline respondents
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and disciplinary criteria governing registered patent practitioners' conflicts of interest, duties to clients, withdrawal obligations, and related sanctions under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct and OED enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct to registered practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Registered practitioners (e.g., Respondent, Reg. No. 30,282) are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct set forth at 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being registered to practice before the USPTO in patent matters subjects an individual to these rules and OED disciplinary jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of USPTO Director/OED over disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19, 11.20, and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory and regulatory provisions authorize OED investigations, settlement agreements, and issuance of Final Orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(1) — prompt client notice when informed consent required
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall promptly inform the client of any decision or circumstance with respect to which the client's informed consent is required by the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to promptly notify a client of circumstances requiring informed consent can constitute a rule violation and is a basis for discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.107 — prohibition on conflicted concurrent representation absent informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent a client if the representation of one client will be directly adverse to another client or if there is a significant risk the representation will be materially limited by responsibilities to another client unless, inter alia, each affected client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent representation that is directly adverse or materially limiting requires written, confirmed informed consent from each affected client; absent that consent, representation is prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.109(a) — prohibition on adverse representation against former clients absent written consent
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner who has formerly represented a client in a matter shall not thereafter represent another person in the same or substantially related matter in which that person's interests are materially adverse to the interests of the former client unless the former client gives informed consent, confirmed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representation against a former client in the same or substantially related matter requires the former client's written informed consent; otherwise the practitioner must decline or obtain waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(a)(1) — duty to withdraw when continuing would violate rules or law
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner shall not represent a client, or where representation has commenced, shall withdraw from the representation of a client if the representation will result in violation of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct or other law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the practitioner knows that continued representation would violate the Rules (for example, due to a conflict or material prior art issue tied to a former client), the practitioner must withdraw.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not file or prosecute claims not patentably distinct from a current or former client's patents without informed consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing and prosecuting patent applications on behalf of a new client containing claims that the practitioner knew or reasonably should have known were not patentably distinct from patents obtained for a current or former client violates the Rules absent informed consent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED treated filing and prosecuting such claims (here, on behalf of Company 2 when Company 1 held related patents the practitioner prosecuted) as a basis for finding violations of §§ 11.104(a)(1), 11.107, 11.109(a), and 11.116(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid drafting specifications that distinguish from a former client's work without written consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishing the invention of a new client's patent application from the invention in a publication or application previously filed and prosecuted for a former client, without obtaining the former client's informed consent, is a Rule violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example in this matter: Respondent drafted language in Company 2's application C distinguishing it from Company 1's published application D (which Respondent had filed/prosecuted), without Company 1's informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw when USPTO determines former client's publication is material prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner must withdraw from representation where continued representation would violate the Rules — for instance, after the examiner determines that a former client's published application is material prior art to the new client's claims, the practitioner must withdraw if continuing would cause a Rules violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to withdraw under those circumstances (here, continued prosecution of application C after the examiner deemed Company 1's publication material) was cited as a violation of § 11.116(a)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent must be confirmed in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Rules permit representation despite a potential conflict, the Rules require that 'informed consent' be given and 'confirmed in writing' by each affected (or former) client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement and Joint Legal Conclusions repeatedly rely on the written-confirmation requirement in §§ 11.107 and 11.109(a) as the necessary procedural safeguard for conflicted representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional obligation to have procedures to identify and address conflicts of interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners should have formal procedures in place to appropriately identify and address conflicts of interest between clients; lack of such procedures was acknowledged by the Respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing appropriate procedures to identify/address conflicts is a mitigating consideration; absence of procedures may contribute to a finding of misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigating and aggravating factors for sanctioning
rubrics_metrics.description: OED considers factors such as length of registered practice, prior disciplinary history, cooperation with investigation, implementation of corrective procedures, and candor when determining sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case, Respondent's 40+ years of registration, no prior disciplinary history, cooperation, and representation that he implemented procedures and now understands the rules were cited as additional considerations that informed the agreed-upon sanction (reprimand).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remedial measures available/ordered by OED
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanctions may include public reprimand, electronic publication of the Final Order in OED's FOIA Reading Room, publication of a notice in the Official Gazette, waiver of appeal rights, and each party bearing its own costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Agreement resulted in an agreed-upon sanction consisting of a reprimand, publication in OED records and the Official Gazette, waiver of rights to seek reconsideration or review, and each party bearing its own costs.
